clauses.reason: The original command is: "I hereby exempt the said Frederick C. Mayer from compulsory retirement for age for an indefinite period of time." Executive Order 10569 of October 5, 1954 amended it by substituting the phrase until December 31, 1954 for the words for an indefinite period of time. Text before: "for an indefinite period of time". Text after: "until December 31, 1954". The amendment substitutes words in the last paragraph and keeps the exemption itself in force, so the clause continued, amended, and ended with the stated day. December 31, 1954 is recorded inclusive, with the exclusive reading (ends as December 31 begins) as the alternative. No held order extends it further, so this is the first end. State on 2026-10-14: terminated.

research_rationale:
EO 10334 (17 FR 2741; signed March 26, 1952; F.R. Doc. 52-3689) exempts Frederick C. Mayer, Organist and Choirmaster at the United States Military Academy, from compulsory retirement for age under section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932 "for an indefinite period of time." As signed, the exemption had no stated end. Executive Order 10569 of October 5, 1954 amended it by substituting the phrase until December 31, 1954 for the words for an indefinite period of time in the last paragraph. Under the 2026-10-21 strike-and-insert ruling the clause continued, amended, and the amendment is a later event that records the text before and after; here the amendment also supplies the only stated end. The first end is therefore December 31, 1954, recorded inclusive under the until-date ruling (the exemption runs through that day), with the exclusive reading (ends as December 31 begins) as the alternative. Both orders are cited to their held Federal Register texts (EO 10334 at 17 FR 2741; EO 10569 at 19 FR 6493, signed October 5, 1954), government printed copies registered in the packet; the quotation for EO 10569 is the packet's registered text of that order.
